issues.t: Engine oil sludge (oil gel)
issues.sym: Oil pressure light, ticking or knocking, rising oil consumption, and in bad cases sudden engine failure, often on cars with stretched oil-change intervals.
issues.why: Oil in these engines could thicken into a gel-like sludge that blocks oil passages. Toyota acknowledged it with a special policy that extended coverage for sludge damage.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on or the engine knocks, stop and have it checked before driving further. Keep oil changes short and use the correct oil.

issues.t: Stripped cylinder head bolt threads
issues.sym: Slow coolant loss with no visible leak, coolant seeping near the back of the engine, overheating, or symptoms that look like a blown head gasket.
issues.why: The head bolt threads in the aluminum engine block can pull out, letting the head gasket lose its clamping force. Toyota published a repair procedure using thread inserts.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. A shop can confirm it and install thread inserts; ignoring it can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky automatic shifts
issues.sym: Hard, clunky shifts, especially the 2-3 upshift or when slowing down, and an occasional jolt when the transmission changes gear.
issues.why: Shift programming in the engine computer caused firm or poorly timed shifts. Toyota released a computer recalibration to smooth shifting.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether the shift recalibration has been done and have the fluid level and condition checked.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: Oil level drops quickly between changes, low-oil warning, blue-tinted exhaust smoke.
issues.why: The piston rings can clog and let oil burn in the cylinders. Toyota ran a warranty enhancement program (ZE7) for it, which has since expired.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and top it off. Do not keep driving with low oil; a shop can confirm with an oil consumption test and discuss a piston and ring repair.

issues.t: Sticky, melting or cracked dashboard
issues.sym: The dash top turns shiny and tacky, gives off glare on the windshield, or cracks.
issues.why: The dashboard material breaks down with heat and humidity. Toyota offered a warranty enhancement program (ZE6) for cracked or sticky dashboards.
issues.next: Mostly cosmetic, but glare can hurt visibility. Ask a dealer whether any coverage still applies; a dash cover is a simple fix.

issues.t: Driver's power window switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Window switch that works on and off, feels sticky or hot, or a burning or melting smell from the driver's door.
issues.why: Uneven lubrication inside the master window switch could make it overheat and melt, creating a fire risk. Toyota recalled the switch.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke from the door, stop using the switch and have it repaired right away.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal can be trapped by floor mat (recall)
issues.sym: Gas pedal stays down or the car keeps accelerating after you lift your foot.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong floor mat could catch the gas pedal. Toyota reshaped the pedal, replaced mats and added brake-override software under recall.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and use only a properly secured, correct mat. If the pedal sticks, brake firmly, shift to Neutral and stop safely.

issues.t: VVT-i oil hose leak
issues.sym: Sudden oil leak at the front of the engine, oil pressure warning light, and abnormal engine noise.
issues.why: The rubber section of the oil hose that feeds the variable valve timing system can break down with age and burst. Toyota ran a service campaign to replace it with a redesigned hose.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Have a dealer check whether the updated line was installed.

issues.t: Hybrid brake actuator or brake control unit failure
issues.sym: Brake and ABS warning lights and a change in how the brakes feel.
issues.why: The hybrid's electronic brake actuator and its control unit and pedal sensor can fail. Toyota extended coverage on these parts with a warranty enhancement program (ZE1).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have the brakes checked promptly when the brake warning lights come on, and ask a dealer about the extended coverage.

issues.t: Shudder at light throttle
issues.sym: A brief vibration or shudder, often around 25-50 mph under light acceleration, as the transmission locks up.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch can engage roughly. Toyota released a software update (LSC E03) and extended torque converter coverage (ZE5) if the update did not cure it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the software update was done. If the shudder remains, the torque converter may need replacing.

issues.t: Water leak onto airbag control module (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, heavy steering from loss of power assist, or in rare cases an airbag going off.
issues.why: A clogged air conditioning drain (spider webs were one cause) could let water drip onto the airbag control module and short it out.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the airbag light comes on or steering suddenly gets heavy, have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Musty or moldy smell from the A/C
issues.sym: A sour or mildew smell from the vents, mostly when the A/C first turns on.
issues.why: Moisture and debris collect on the A/C evaporator and allow mold to grow. Owners filed a class action over it, and part of it has been settled.
issues.next: Replace the cabin filter and have the evaporator cleaned. Ask a dealer about any A/C odor bulletins or settlement coverage.

issues.t: Rough or hesitant shifting
issues.sym: Harsh engagement into gear when cold, abrupt 1-2 shifts, hunting for gears, or hesitation pulling away.
issues.why: Shift programming on the 8-speed automatic. Toyota issued bulletins to reprogram the engine and transmission computer.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether the latest software update has been applied, and report it again if shifting stays harsh.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, failure to start, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank could stop working. Toyota recalled it and replaces the pump.
issues.next: Check the VIN for these recalls and get the pump replaced. A stall at speed is dangerous, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump failure (recall)
issues.sym: Brake pedal suddenly gets hard and the car takes much longer to stop, sometimes with a brake warning.
issues.why: Part of the engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can wear and break, cutting off power assist. On some 2018 Camrys an oil passage in the vacuum pump was machined wrong, so brake assist can cut out suddenly (recall 18V-211).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for this recall. If the pedal turns hard, press much harder, stop safely and have the car repaired before driving on.

issues.t: Tail light bulb holder can lose contact (recall)
issues.sym: A tail or brake light that flickers or stops working even with a good bulb.
issues.why: The plastic bulb holder was not heat resistant enough, so it can deform and let the bulb lose its electrical contact.
issues.next: Have a helper check your rear lights. A dealer can confirm whether the recall was done on your car; otherwise the bulb holder is a simple replacement.

issues.t: Key can be removed when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out of the ignition with the shifter still in gear, so the car can roll after you walk away.
issues.why: A lock pin in the key interlock solenoid can jam, defeating the feature that holds the key until the shifter is in Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and ask a Toyota dealer to check whether this recall is still open on your car.

issues.t: Accelerator cable can wear through on V6 cruise control cars (recall)
issues.sym: The engine keeps pulling or the speed does not drop when you lift off the gas pedal.
issues.why: On V6 cars with cruise control, the accelerator cable housing can deform where it meets the cruise actuator, letting the inner cable fray and hang up.
issues.next: If the throttle ever sticks, brake firmly, shift to Neutral and pull over. Do not keep driving until a dealer has checked the cable and the recall status.

issues.t: Rear axle part may be weak from improper heat treatment (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning. A grinding or clunking from a rear wheel, or a rear wheel that looks tilted, is a serious sign.
issues.why: Some rear axle shafts were not heat treated correctly at the factory and can break.
issues.next: Have a dealer run the VIN for this recall. If a rear wheel makes new noises or looks out of position, stop driving and have the car towed.

issues.t: Front subframe may be poorly welded (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, wandering steering or uneven tire wear that keeps coming back, usually after many years of use.
issues.why: On some cars the front subframe, which carries the engine and front suspension, did not get adequate welds and can fail over time.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the front end clunks or the steering feels loose, have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may be twisted (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you would notice while driving. The problem only shows up in a side crash.
issues.why: On cars with curtain airbags, the folded bag could be twisted near its inflator during assembly, which slows it down when it fires.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a Toyota dealer and have the recall inspection done if it is still open.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley outer ring can slip on V6 engines (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or chirp from the belts, a belt that comes off, and steering that suddenly gets heavy.
issues.why: The outer ring of the crankshaft pulley was bonded with too little adhesive. It can shift out of line and throw the power steering belt.
issues.next: If the steering turns heavy or a belt comes off, pull over and have it repaired. Ask a dealer whether the pulley recall has been done.

issues.t: Windshield wiper switch can short out (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers that stop working or act up, sometimes in the rain when you need them.
issues.why: The wiper switch assembly on the steering column can develop an internal short.
issues.next: Have the recall done at a Toyota dealer. If the wipers quit in bad weather, pull over until you can see safely.

issues.t: Front lower control arm can separate from ball joint (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the left front, loose steering, or a front wheel that suddenly folds outward.
issues.why: Some left front lower arms were made without the proper clamping area for the ball joint bolt, so the joint can work loose.
issues.next: Check the VIN right away. If you hear front-end clunks, stop driving and have the car inspected.

issues.t: Fuel delivery pipe may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell from under the hood, sometimes with a visible wet spot on the engine.
issues.why: The pipe that feeds fuel to the injectors can leak, and fuel on a hot engine can catch fire.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have the car towed to a dealer. Check the VIN for this recall either way.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out (recall)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes heavy, usually with a power steering warning light.
issues.why: A part inside the electric power steering computer was damaged during manufacturing and can fail.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. You can still steer with more effort. Slow down, pull over when safe, and have a dealer check the recall status.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor miscalibrated (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may not match who is sitting in the seat.
issues.why: The seat sensor that classifies the front passenger was not calibrated correctly on cars built over a few months, so the airbags may not fire as intended.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check the VIN and recalibrate the sensor if the recall is open.

issues.t: Passenger knee airbag attached with wrong fasteners (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing noticeable in normal driving.
issues.why: On cars from a short build window, the front passenger knee airbag was installed with incorrect fasteners that can loosen and affect how the bag deploys.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a dealer and have the fasteners replaced if the recall applies.

issues.t: Oversized pistons can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, engine noise, smoke, a warning light, or the engine shutting off while driving.
issues.why: A small batch of 2.5L engines was built with pistons larger than specified, which can damage the engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If the engine runs rough or stalls, stop driving. Have a dealer check the VIN; affected engines were replaced.

issues.t: V6 fuel pipes may not be fully connected (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: On some V6 cars the fuel delivery pipes were not properly joined to their hoses at the factory, so fuel can leak near hot parts.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside, do not drive, and have the car towed to a dealer. Check the VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Engine can leak coolant from porous castings (recall)
issues.sym: Dropping coolant level, temperature warning, sweet smell, or the engine stalling. Coolant may also get inside the engine.
issues.why: Some 2.5L engine castings were porous and can crack, leaking coolant inside or outside the engine. That can lead to overheating, oil leaks and a fire risk.
issues.next: If the temperature warning comes on or coolant keeps disappearing, stop driving. Have a dealer check the VIN; affected engines were inspected and replaced.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor can short and disable the airbag (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or a passenger airbag status light that is wrong for the person seated.
issues.why: The sensors in the front passenger seat that detect an occupant can short circuit, which may stop the passenger airbag from deploying.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a Toyota dealer and have the sensors inspected or replaced.

issues.t: Wheel lug nuts may be loose (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or knocking from a wheel, vibration that gets worse, or a wheel that wobbles.
issues.why: On a limited group of cars the lug nuts may not have been tightened properly, so a wheel can come off.
issues.next: Toyota advised owners of affected cars not to drive until repaired. Check the VIN, and have the lug nuts torqued before driving if it applies.

issues.t: Rear seat head restraint brackets may be weakly welded (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing; a rear head restraint may feel loose or rattle.
issues.why: The brackets that hold the second-row head restraints did not get strong enough welds on some cars, so they may not protect a rear passenger in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a dealer and have the rear seat back parts replaced if the recall is open.

issues.t: Hybrid inverter bolt may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A hybrid system warning appears and the car can suddenly lose drive power while you are moving.
issues.why: A bolt inside the inverter may not have been tightened at the factory, so the connection can arc, short out and in the worst case start a fire.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the VIN and carry out the recall right away; do not put off driving it in for this one.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank after starting (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge screen stays dark when you start the car, and the turn signal and hazard indicators, seat belt reminder and key reminder do not show.
issues.why: A software fault in the instrument display keeps it from waking up properly at start-up.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Get the free software update at a Toyota dealer; until then watch your speed closely, since the speedometer may not be visible.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak
issues.sym: A burnt oil smell after driving, oil spots on the engine or a slow drop in the oil level, often with no puddle on the ground.
issues.why: The rubber gasket under the valve cover hardens with heat and age and stops sealing, so oil seeps out of the top of the engine.
issues.next: Have the gasket replaced and keep an eye on the oil level in the meantime; it is a slow leak but it can drip onto hot parts and smoke.

issues.t: Knocking from worn front strut mounts and sway bar links
issues.sym: Knocking, clunking or rattling from the front end over bumps and rough pavement, sometimes felt through the steering wheel.
issues.why: The rubber in the strut mounts and the small stabilizer bar links wears out, so metal parts move against each other.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected soon; worn mounts and links change how the car handles and should not be left for long.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: A sweet smell, pink or green drips near the front of the engine, low coolant in the tank and the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: The seal and bearing in the water pump wear out and let coolant escape where the pump bolts to the engine.
issues.next: Get it replaced before it fails completely, because losing coolant can overheat and ruin the engine. On V6 models the timing belt comes off for this job.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: A battery shaped warning light while driving, dimming lights, a slow crank the next morning or the car dying on the road.
issues.why: The brushes and bearings inside the alternator wear out, so it no longer keeps the battery charged.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested and the alternator replaced; once the light is on you may only have a short distance left.

issues.t: Front oxygen sensor fails and lights the check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light, slightly worse gas mileage and sometimes a rough or hesitant feel at light throttle.
issues.why: The front air/fuel ratio sensor in the exhaust ages and stops reporting accurately, so the engine computer sets a code.
issues.next: Have the code read and the sensor replaced; it is not urgent, but a lazy sensor wastes fuel and can fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Knocking or popping from the moonroof area
issues.sym: A knock, pop, tick or snap comes from the roof near the windshield as you drive over bumps and uneven pavement.
issues.why: Parts of the moonroof assembly shift and rub against each other. Toyota published a revised repair for the noise.
issues.next: This is not a safety problem. A dealer or body shop can carry out the bulletin repair if the noise bothers you.

issues.t: Squeak from the front stabilizer bar bushings
issues.sym: A dry squeak or creak from the front of the car at low speed, worst over driveways, speed bumps and dips.
issues.why: The rubber bushings that hold the front stabilizer bar lose their lubrication and bind on the bar as it twists.
issues.next: Usually not urgent, but have the noise checked to confirm the cause. The bushings can be lubricated or replaced the way the Toyota bulletin describes.

issues.t: Check Brake System message at startup
issues.sym: A brake system message and warning lights appear when you start the car, and sometimes clear on their own after a while.
issues.why: The brake control unit stores fault codes, usually traced to a sensor or its wiring. Toyota published a diagnostic bulletin for this exact complaint.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have the stored codes read. The brakes normally still work, but while the message is there it hides any real brake fault, so do not leave it.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fluid leak at the oil pan gasket
issues.sym: Red fluid drips or a damp film builds up on the bottom of the transmission, and you may find small spots where you park.
issues.why: The gasket between the transmission oil pan and the case seeps. Toyota covered it in a bulletin with a revised sealing procedure.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the pan resealed. If the fluid gets low the transmission can start slipping, which is a much bigger bill.

issues.t: Hybrid battery cooling fan clogged with dust
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on in a hybrid, often with a hybrid system warning, and the fan behind the rear seat may run louder or longer than usual.
issues.why: Dust and debris collect in the hybrid battery cooling fan and its duct, so the battery pack runs warmer and the control system logs a fault.
issues.next: Have the fan and duct cleaned as the Toyota bulletin describes. Letting the pack run hot shortens its life.
